newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine banks show strong 9-mth earnings.
newsitem.headline: Philippine banks show strong 9-mth earnings.

text.p: Big Philippine banks continued to show strong nine-month earnings growth on the back of a robust economy and their stocks would continue to be good buys, analysts said on Thursday.
Since the nine months results reporting season began this week, two of three big banks reported good results.
The only laggard was the newly-privatised Philippine National Bank which reported lower than expected profits due to a bloated workforce and some bad loans.

"We'll see some market weakness (on PNB) tomorrow. But there seems to be positive news. It's loan and deposit growth are picking up which should augur well for PNB," said Jose Mario Cuyegkeng, research head of ING Barings Securities.
"PNB is just turning around. It's just that expectations were really high on its first year as a private bank," he added.

But with the recent sale of big bank-owned assets in the third quarter, PNB should have a steady stream of good earnings next year as proceeds from the sale are rechanneled to hike lending, Cuyegkeng said.

PNB, the biggest bank in terms of assets, reported on Thursday its net profit surged by 156 percent to 3.433 billion pesos in the nine-month period, primarily due to a non-recurring gain of 3.790 billion pesos from the sale of bank-owned assets and a provision for valuation reserve of 1.350 billion pesos.
Stripped of those extraordinaries, PNB posted a net income from regular operations of 993 million pesos, just four percent higher than last year.
PNB said it was cutting its net income target from regular operations this year to 1.7 billion from 2.0 billion pesos.
Metrobank's announcement of a 39.5 percent growth in net profit to 3.189 billion pesos from January to September versus the year-ago 2.286 billion pesos was hailed by analysts.
"Metrobank is in line with our forecast of 5.1 billion pesos," Queensie de los Reyes, analyst at DBP-Daiwa Securities said.
"We like Metrobank," said Raul Ruiz, vice president of Sun Hung Kai Securities, since it has a strong presence in the consumer banking business.
"It (Metrobank) is still part of the core holding in a portfolio but the potential upside in its price is limited because it is trading at a premium," said ING Baring's Cuyegkeng.

BPI, the third biggest bank in the country, reported a third quarter net income of 913.741 million pesos, which took its nine-month net to 2.454 billion pesos, a 63 percent jump from 1.506 billion pesos in the same period in 1995.
BPI had projected its combined profits with CityTrust Banking Corp for the full-year 1996 would reach 4.0 billion pesos. The merger with CityTrust took effect on October 7.
"BPI is looking good. It's 4.0 billion-peso net income target is realistic," said Sun Hung Kai's Ruiz.
"I think it (the 4.0 billion pesos) will be exceeded," said DBP-Daiwa's De los Reyes.

Ruiz added BPI's secondary offer which would begin on Friday would improve the liquidity of BPI shares. He estimated BPI's free float would increase to 24 percent from 20 percent after the secondary offer.
